Dated 4 November 2025. Effective from 15 November 2025, the start date of the Services Agreement. Governed by the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 1. Subject matter and duration

1.1 Sorrel processes personal data to verify the identity of the directors, beneficial owners and authorised users of businesses that apply to become Kestrel merchants, and to screen them against sanctions and politically exposed person (PEP) lists.

1.2 This agreement lasts as long as the Services Agreement, and clauses 10 and 11 survive its end.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 2. Instructions

2.1 Sorrel processes Kestrel personal data only on Kestrel's documented instructions. Those instructions are the service description in Annex 1 and the API requests Kestrel sends.

2.2 Sorrel will tell Kestrel at once if it thinks an instruction breaks data protection law, and may pause that processing until Kestrel confirms or changes the instruction.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 3. What is processed (Annex 1)

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Data subjects | Directors, beneficial owners and authorised users of merchant applicants and merchants |
| Personal data | Name, date of birth, home address, nationality, ID document number and images, selfie video, IP address and device data captured during the check |
| Special category data | Biometric data (face templates) used only to match the selfie to the ID document |
| Purpose | Customer due diligence under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017; sanctions screening |
| Kestrel's lawful basis | Legal obligation; for biometric data, the substantial public interest condition for preventing or detecting unlawful acts in Schedule 1 of the Data Protection Act 2018 |
| Volume | About 5,000 checks a month |

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 4. Retention by Sorrel

| Data | How long Sorrel keeps it |
| --- | --- |
| ID document images and selfie video | 30 days after the check, then deleted |
| Biometric face templates | Deleted as soon as the match result is returned, and never kept longer than 24 hours |
| Check results, extracted document fields and audit log | Returned to Kestrel; Sorrel keeps a copy for 90 days for support, then deletes it |
| Sanctions and PEP screening results | Returned to Kestrel; Sorrel keeps a copy for 90 days |

Kestrel keeps check and screening results for 5 years after the end of the business relationship, as the Money Laundering Regulations require. That retention is Kestrel's responsibility as controller.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 5. Security

5.1 Sorrel will keep ISO 27001 certification for the services and give Kestrel its SOC 2 Type II report once a year.

5.2 Personal data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher). Sorrel hosts the service in the AWS eu-west-2 (London) region.

5.3 Only named Sorrel staff with a need may access Kestrel data, and every access is logged. Sorrel runs an external penetration test each year and sends Kestrel a summary of findings within 30 days.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 6. Sub-processors

6.1 Kestrel approves the sub-processors below.

| Sub-processor | Service | Location | Transfer safeguard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL | Hosting in the AWS eu-west-2 (London) region | United Kingdom | None needed |
| Lantern Screening B.V. | Sanctions and PEP list screening | Netherlands | UK adequacy regulations for the EEA |
| Kittle Labs Inc. | Support for the liveness detection model; sees images only for escalated cases, no more than 50 a month | United States | UK International Data Transfer Addendum to the EU standard contractual clauses; transfer risk assessment dated 20 October 2025 |

6.2 Sorrel will give Kestrel at least 30 days' written notice before adding or replacing a sub-processor. Kestrel may object on reasonable grounds. If the parties cannot agree within 30 days, Kestrel may end the affected services without paying any termination charge.

6.3 Sorrel stays fully liable to Kestrel for the acts of its sub-processors.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 7. Personal data breaches

7.1 Sorrel will notify Kestrel of any personal data breach without undue delay, and in any case within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, by email to privacy@kestrelpay.example and by phone to Kestrel's security on-call number.

7.2 Within 72 hours Sorrel will send what it knows of the nature of the breach, the data and people affected, the likely consequences and the steps taken.

7.3 Kestrel decides whether to notify the Information Commissioner's Office and the people affected. Sorrel will not notify anyone about a breach of Kestrel data without Kestrel's agreement, unless the law requires it.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 8. Data subject rights

Sorrel will pass any request from a data subject to Kestrel within 2 business days and will not answer it directly. Sorrel will help Kestrel respond within the time limits in the UK GDPR.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 9. Audits

9.1 Kestrel, or an auditor it appoints, may audit Sorrel's compliance with this agreement once in each contract year on 30 days' notice, and at any time after a personal data breach.

9.2 Sorrel will give the FCA and the ICO any access they ask for.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 10. Return and deletion

When the Services Agreement ends, Sorrel will delete all Kestrel personal data within 30 days, unless the law requires it to keep some, and will send a written certificate of deletion signed by its Data Protection Officer.

chunks.title: KPC-2025-0231 Sorrel Identity DPA.docx
chunks.text:
## 11. Liability

Liability under this agreement follows clause 12 of the Services Agreement, except that each party's total liability for breaches of this agreement is limited to £2,000,000 in each contract year.

## 2. Safeguarding

Kestrel safeguards relevant funds by segregation, in designated safeguarding accounts at Albion Clearing Bank (GBP) and Banco Meridional, S.A. (EUR). At 30 June 2026 Kestrel Pay Ltd held £1.02bn of customer funds: £0.94bn in GBP and €95m (about £0.08bn) in EUR. Kestrel Pay Europe Ltd held a further £0.22bn, so the group total was £1.24bn.

The FCA's new safeguarding rules came into force on 7 May 2026. They add a monthly safeguarding return and require the resolution pack to be kept up to date. Finance updated the safeguarding reconciliation procedure to version 3.1 from the same date.

Daily reconciliations. There were 61 UK business days in Q2. All 61 reconciliations were finished by the 11:00 deadline, and none showed a shortfall.

Q1 breach, now closed. On Thursday 12 March the EUR reconciliation was finished at 11:20, after the deadline, because the reconciliation tool could not load a bank statement file after the bank changed its file format. There was no shortfall. We reported the breach to the FCA on 13 March (SG-2026-01). Treasury Operations now checks at 15:00 every business day that each bank's statement file has arrived.

Monthly returns. The first monthly safeguarding return (May) was submitted on 12 June. The June return was submitted on 14 July, ahead of the deadline of 21 July.

Annual audit. Fernside & Co LLP, our safeguarding auditor since October 2025, completed the audit for 2025 on 27 March 2026. It gave a reasonable assurance opinion with two low-rated findings, both closed by 30 April. Interim fieldwork for the 2026 audit (KPC-2026-0326) has been brought forward to 7 to 25

September 2026.

# Customer Success Escalation Guide

Owner: Hannah Kim, Customer Success Manager. Reviewed by Sofia Lindqvist (Compliance) for sections 5 and 6. Last updated 28 August 2026.

This guide tells Support and Customer Success when and how to escalate a merchant problem, and what to say while we fix it.

chunks.title: Customer Success Escalation Guide.pdf
chunks.text:
## 1. Priorities and response targets

| Priority | Definition | First response | Updates | Hours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Merchant cannot take card payments, or cannot pay staff on pay day | 30 minutes | Every hour | 24/7 |
| P2 | A product is degraded or partly failing for the merchant | 4 business hours | Every business day | Support hours |
| P3 | Question, how-to, or a problem with a workaround | 1 business day | When there is news | Support hours |
| P4 | Feature request or feedback | 5 business days | None | Support hours |

Support hours are 07:00 to 22:00 UK time, 7 days a week. Support works from the London and Lisbon offices on weekdays and from home at weekends, when the offices are closed. P1 cases outside those hours go straight to the Payments on-call engineer through PagerDuty.

chunks.title: Customer Success Escalation Guide.pdf
chunks.text:
## 2. Tiers

| Tier | Who | Handles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1 | Support team | All new cases, known issues, how-to questions |
| Tier 2 | Customer Success Managers (Hannah Kim leads) | P1 and P2 cases, complaints, credits, anything Tier 1 cannot solve in 1 business day |
| Tier 3 | Engineering on call, through the incident process | Suspected outages, bugs, data problems |

chunks.title: Customer Success Escalation Guide.pdf
chunks.text:
## 3. When to escalate to Engineering

Raise an incident (page Payments on-call) when any of these happen:

- 3 or more merchants report the same error within 15 minutes.

- Merchants report KP-9001, KP-9003 or KP-9007 in growing numbers.

- A payroll payout batch is stuck on pay day.

- Merchants report customers charged twice.

- The status page shows nothing but merchants say the Dashboard or API is down.

Do not wait to be sure. The on-call engineer would rather close a false alarm than miss an outage.

chunks.title: Customer Success Escalation Guide.pdf
chunks.text:
## 4. Error codes Support sees most

| Code | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| KP-3002 | Account restricted. Do not explain or guess why. Say: "Our team is reviewing the account and will contact you." Send the case to Compliance (Sofia Lindqvist) the same day. |
| KP-4031 | Soft decline, needs 3-D Secure. If one merchant sees a lot of these, their integration is probably not sending 3-D Secure; pass it to Ravi Shah, Sales Engineer. |
| KP-4040 | Blocked by fraud screening. Never say which rule fired or why. Offer the review form; Risk Operations answers within 1 business day. |
| KP-5003, KP-5004 | Confirmation of Payee. The merchant must check the payee's details. We cannot override a no match. |
| KP-5021 | Payment scheme down. Payouts retry for 4 hours on their own. Escalate as P1 if it is pay day. |
| KP-9007 | Acquirer timeout, outcome unknown. Tell the merchant to check the payment status before retrying, and to retry only with the same idempotency key. A retry with a new key can charge the customer twice. |

The full list is in the Payments API Error Code Catalogue in /Engineering/Runbooks. Ask Payments Engineering for anything not covered here.

chunks.title: Customer Success Escalation Guide.pdf
chunks.text:
## 5. Complaints

A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction, spoken or written, about our service, whether or not the merchant uses the word "complaint".

| 1. Log it in the complaints register on the day you receive it. |
| --- |
| 2. Acknowledge it in writing within 1 business day. |
| 3. Send a final response within 15 business days. In exceptional cases, send a holding reply by day 15 that explains the delay, and a final response by day 35. |
| 4. The final response must tell eligible merchants (micro-enterprises and small businesses) that they can refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service within 6 months. |
| Sofia Lindqvist reviews the register every month and reports themes to the Exec. |

chunks.title: Customer Success Escalation Guide.pdf
chunks.text:
## 6. What never to say

- Why an account is restricted or under review. This can be tipping off, which is a criminal offence.

- Which fraud rule blocked a payment, or any threshold.

- That a problem is "the acquirer's fault" or names a supplier, before Engineering confirms it.

- Promises of a fix time that Engineering has not given you.

chunks.title: Customer Success Escalation Guide.pdf
chunks.text:
## 7. Credits and goodwill

### 7.1 Checkout Pro service credits

Checkout Pro has a 99.95% monthly availability commitment. If availability falls below it, every affected Checkout Pro merchant gets a credit on the next invoice:

| Monthly availability | Credit |
| --- | --- |
| 99.0% to below 99.95% | 10% of the monthly fee |
| 95.0% to below 99.0% | 25% of the monthly fee |
| Below 95.0% | 50% of the monthly fee |

Engineering confirms availability after each incident. Customer Success sends Finance AP the list of affected merchants, and the credits appear automatically on the next invoice. For INC-2026-0817 on 17 August 2026, August availability was 99.89%, so the 610 affected Checkout Pro merchants get a 10%

credit on their August invoice, due out on 5 September.

chunks.title: Customer Success Escalation Guide.pdf
chunks.text:
### 7.2 Goodwill credits

| Who | Limit per merchant per quarter |
| --- | --- |
| Customer Success Manager | £100 |
| Head of Sales | £500 |
| CFO | Above £500 |

Record every goodwill credit in the CRM with the reason. Goodwill credits are not an admission of fault; say "as a gesture of goodwill".

chunks.title: Customer Success Escalation Guide.pdf
chunks.text:
## 8. Status page wording

Use these first messages and update them as you learn more:

- Investigating: "Some card payments are failing. We are investigating and will update this page within 30 minutes."

- Identified: "We have found the cause and are working on a fix."

- Monitoring: "Card payments have recovered. We are monitoring."

- Resolved: "This incident is resolved. If you saw duplicate charges, they will be reversed automatically within 2 business days."

This is how we find, qualify and close merchants, and how we hand them to Customer Success. Read it in your first month, together with the price list and the Pricing FAQ.

chunks.title: Sales Playbook 2026.docx
chunks.text:
## 1. Who we sell to

### 1.1 Good fit

- Small and medium businesses in the UK and the EU with £500,000 to £50m annual turnover and 5 to 250 staff.

- Card volume between £20,000 and £5m a month.

- Best verticals: hospitality (especially multi-site cafés and restaurants), e-commerce, professional services, and retail chains with up to 50 sites.

- Businesses that need more than one of our products. A merchant using Checkout and Accounts stays more than twice as long as one using Checkout alone.

chunks.title: Sales Playbook 2026.docx
chunks.text:
### 1.2 Not a fit

- Prohibited and high-risk categories: gambling, crypto exchanges, adult content, weapons, CBD and debt collection. Do not start a conversation; log the lead as "not eligible".

- Businesses with more than £100m a year in card volume. We are not built for enterprise integrations.

- Businesses registered outside the UK and the EEA.

If you are not sure whether a business is eligible, ask Compliance before the first demo, not after the proposal.

# Pricing FAQ for Sales and Customer Success

chunks.text:
## Plans and SKUs

What is the difference between KC-STD-01 and KC-STD-12? Both are Checkout Standard with no monthly fee. KC-STD-01 is monthly rolling at 1.49% + 20p for UK and EEA consumer cards. KC-STD-12 is a 12-month term at 1.39% + 20p. Non-UK, non-EEA and commercial cards are 2.49% + 20p on KC-STD-01 and 2.39% + 20p on KC-STD-12.

When should a merchant move to Checkout Pro? Checkout Pro costs £49 a month on KC-PRO-01 or £39 a month on KC-PRO-12, and charges 1.19% + 15p or 1.09% + 15p. On UK consumer cards, KC-PRO-12 is cheaper than KC-STD-12 once a merchant processes about £9,200 a month at an average ticket of £40. Pro also brings the 99.95% availability commitment, same-day settlement to a Kestrel Accounts balance and the £20,000 single transaction limit.

Why did KC-PRO-01 go up? It rose from £45 to £49 a month on 1 April 2026 (price list 2026.2). Like every 2026.2 change, the new price applies to new contracts and renewals only, so merchants already on KC-PRO-01 keep £45 until they renew. KC-PRO-12 stayed at £39.

Can a merchant switch from monthly to a 12-month plan mid-month? Yes. The 12-month term starts on the day of the switch, and the first invoice is pro-rated. A move the other way, from 12 months to monthly, counts as ending the 12-month plan early.

What does it cost to leave a 12-month plan early? The remaining monthly fees for the term, capped at £300 or €350 per plan. KC-STD-12 has no monthly fee, so leaving it early costs nothing; the merchant simply goes back to KC-STD-01 rates.

chunks.title: Pricing FAQ.pdf
chunks.text:
## Terminals

Rent or buy a terminal? KC-TERM-01 rents a Kestrel Tap T2 for £15 a month per device, with free replacement. KC-TERM-BUY is a one-off £149 per device with a 12-month warranty. Buying pays back after 10 months, so recommend buying to merchants who expect to stay longer than a year.

Can we give terminal rental free? Up to 3 free months of KC-TERM-01 per site, only for merchants signing KC-PRO-12, and only with Head of Sales approval.

chunks.title: Pricing FAQ.pdf
chunks.text:
## Accounts and Payouts

Is KA-PLUS-12 billed monthly? No. KA-PLUS-12 is £12 a month billed yearly in advance, so the merchant pays £144 (or €168) at the start of the term. KA-PLUS-01 is £14 a month billed monthly.

How much is an extra card? KA-CARD-01 is £3 (€3.50) a month per card beyond the plan's allowance. It was £2.50 before 1 April 2026.

What happens when a KP-BULK-500 merchant sends more than 500 payouts? The first 500 payouts each month are covered by the £125 fee. Each extra payout costs 30p (€0.35). Unused payouts do not roll over. If a merchant regularly sends more than about 1,420 payouts a month, KP-BULK-2000 at £400 is cheaper.

What about pay as you go? KP-PAYG-01 has no monthly fee and charges 35p per UK payout or €0.45 per SEPA payout. It is cheaper than KP-BULK-500 below 357 payouts a month.

Can merchants pay suppliers abroad? Yes, with the KP-FX-01 add-on: 0.6% above the mid-market rate, minimum £2 per payout.

Is KP-BULK-500 the same as error KP-500? No. SKUs always have letters after the prefix (KP-BULK-500). Payments API error codes are four digits (for example KP-5003). There is no code KP-500.

Any transaction rate below the plan rate is a non-standard pricing term: it goes through deal desk to the CFO. Nothing goes below the floor of 0.95% + 10p.

### 3.3 Taxis

Taxis are reimbursed when you travel after 21:00, when you carry equipment or supplies between clinics, or when no reasonable public transport exists. Record the reason in the claim.

chunks.text:
### 3.4 Using your own car

Mileage is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that. Travel between home and your base clinic is not business mileage. If you go from home to a clinic that is not your base, claim the extra distance only. Parking is reimbursed with a receipt. Fines are never reimbursed.

## 4. Limits

The limits apply per person, anywhere in the UK, including London.

| Item | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Meals and subsistence | £25 a day |
| Hotel, any UK city | £150 a night |
| Training courses and conferences | Pre-approved by your line manager and the Operations Director |
| Team meals | Not reimbursed |
| Home working equipment | Not reimbursed; ask IT for a loan item |

chunks.title: Travel and Expenses Policy.pdf
chunks.text:
### 4.1 Meals and subsistence

You can claim meals when you travel overnight on Harbour business, or when you attend training or a meeting away from your base clinic for more than 8 hours in a day. The daily limit covers breakfast, lunch, dinner and soft drinks. Alcohol is not reimbursed.

If breakfast is included in your hotel rate, the daily limit stays the same.

chunks.title: Travel and Expenses Policy.pdf
chunks.text:
### 4.2 Hotels

Overnight stays need approval from the Operations Director before you book. The nightly limit covers the room and taxes. It does not cover the minibar, room service beyond the meals limit, films or late checkout.

## 5. Receipts

Keep an itemised receipt for every expense above £10. Upload a photo of it to the claim. For expenses of £10 or less, such as a bus fare, you can claim without a receipt, but you must enter the date and the business reason.

A card statement is not an itemised receipt. If you lose a receipt, complete the missing receipt form and ask your line manager to sign it.

## 6. Claiming and approval

| 1. Submit claims on the Harbour expenses form, saved next to this policy in the Policies folder, to finance@harbourhealth.example within 30 days of the date you spent the money. |
| --- |
| 2. Your line manager approves every claim. |
| 3. A claim over £250 also needs approval from the Operations Director. |
| 4. Approvers must not approve their own claims. Send those to the Operations Director, or to the Finance Officer if the claim is the Operations Director's. |
| Claims approved by the 10th of the month are paid with that month's salary. Claims approved after the 10th are paid the following month. |

## 7. What is not reimbursed

- Travel between home and your base clinic

- Fines, penalties and parking tickets

- Upgrades to rail or hotels

- Travel or meals for partners, family or friends

- Alcohol

- Gifts for colleagues

- Lost or stolen personal items

## 8. Breaches

Claiming money you did not spend, claiming the same cost twice, or splitting a cost to get under an approval threshold is a disciplinary matter and may be treated as gross misconduct.
